data.name: Ladonna
data.gender_notes: Ladonna is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name Ladonis, meaning 'lady' or 'mistress'. In Greek mythology, the name was associated with the god Pan and the nymphs of his court. In Christian tradition, the name Ladonna is a feminine form of the biblical Ladon, who was a Levite and the father of Abihud. The name Ladonna carries the meaning “Lady, princes, or mistress” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Ladonna usually hope their child will grow to embody lady, princes, or mistress and live with faith, good character and purpose.

It has been used since ancient times as a term of respect and admiration, representing the status and authority of a woman. In Christian tradition, the name carries an additional layer of significance as a feminine form of the biblical name Ladon, which is rooted in the religious history of Judaism and Christianity.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ladonna embodies a powerful spiritual message, reflecting the strength and dignity of a woman rooted in her faith. As a derivative of the Greek word 'ladon', meaning 'lady' or 'mistress', Ladonna signifies the sacred role of women in both the secular and spiritual realms. In Christian tradition, the name invokes the reverence and respect for the strong biblical figure of Ladon, and the important role of women in shaping the course of Jewish and Christian history. Ultimately, the name Ladonna represents a connection to a proud and unyielding legacy of faith, courage, and resilience.
